You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: If a GitLab team member in the US is taking a parental leave of 4 months, what should the manager do with their tasks and output during that time?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): Use internal resources who may be eligible for an interim bonus, and/or consider hiring a temporary contractor.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Korea Limited Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Extended Parental Leave (Child Care Leave)]
Up to one year of additional leave for ongoing childcare needs, available to eligible parents. Extended leave of up to 18 months may be available in certain circumstances.

Eligibility Requirements

- Minimum of six months of GitLab employment prior to scheduled leave start date
- Child must be eight years old or younger, or in second grade or below in elementary school
- Pregnant employees may apply to protect their pregnancy
- Parents cannot take leave simultaneously

Leave Entitlement

- **Duration**: Up to one year per parent
- **Extended Duration**: Up to 18 months total for parents who qualify under any of the following:

- Both parents have taken at least three months of childcare leave each for the same child
- Single parents as defined under the Single-Parent Family Support Act
- Parents of a child with a qualifying disability as prescribed by the Ministry of Employment and Labor

- **Insurance Support**: 40% salary from Employment Insurance Fund
- **GitLab Supplement**: Additional support to reach 100% pay for up to 16 weeks (if eligible under [GitLab's Parental Leave policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/#gitlab-parental-leave))

[Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Eligibility, Entitlement and Planning Your Leave > Returning to Work at 50% Capacity]
Returning to work after parental leave can be challenging as you balance new family responsibilities while reintegrating into a workplace that has evolved during your absence.

To support this transition, GitLab offers team members the option to return at 50% capacity. This program is not tracked in Workday and does not require the Absence Management team’s review or approval. To utilize this benefit:

- Discuss with your manager before starting leave or a few weeks prior to returning
- Work together to determine a schedule that works for both you and your team
- The standard guideline is two to four weeks at reduced capacity, though this can be adjusted based on individual needs
- The 50% figure is flexible, and doesn’t always have to equate to working hours. Some options to consider would be:
  - Adjusting the workload so you’re slowly ramping back up to a full plate - this won’t look the same for everyone - some team members may prefer to ramp up more quickly
  - Adjust the working days/hours so instead of working 5-8hrs days it could be 4-10hrs, or you work really early in the morning/late in the evening
  - Slowly increase the number of working days each week (i.e. 2 days the first week, 3 days the second, etc.)

This transition period gives you space to adjust to your new normal without the pressure of a full workload, allowing time to resolve any unexpected childcare challenges or other family adjustments.

[Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave]
*GitLab’s paid Parental Leave is available for any active team member (regardless of gender) who becomes a parent through childbirth or adoption while working at GitLab. The information in this section is specific to GitLab’s 16-week paid Parental Leave. Different countries or US states may provide team members with their own statutory Parental Leave benefits. Please review your [country/state](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#entity-specific-benefits) Parental Leave benefits for more information on how to apply and tenure requirements (if applicable).*

[Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Eligibility, Entitlement and Planning Your Leave]
GitLab's Parental Leave is available for any active team member (regardless of gender) who becomes a parent through childbirth, adoption, fostering, or surrogacy (intended parent) while working at GitLab. This benefit is available from your first day of employment, provided your child was born, newly adopted, newly placed in your foster care, or born via surrogacy during your employment at GitLab.

GitLab provides 16 weeks of paid Parental Leave, which must be used prior to the child's first birthday, the first anniversary of the adoption, the first anniversary of the foster placement, or the first anniversary of the birth (for surrogacy). Team members are encouraged to decide for themselves how much time they'd like to take, but there are some parameters to keep in mind when planning your leave:

[GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family leaves > Maternity Leave]
Leave Entitlement

- Team members must have continuous employment with GitLab for at least 26 weeks leading up to the "qualifying week" (15th week before the expected week of childbirth)
- Up to 52 weeks leave available
- First 39 weeks paid (combining statutory and GitLab benefits)
- 90% of average earnings for first 6 weeks (before tax), then statutory rate (£194.32/week) or 90% (whichever is lower) of the team member's average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks. This also applies to the leave amounts provided for Parental Leave and Adoption Leave.
- GitLab's enhanced policy provides up to 16 weeks at 100% salary

How to Apply

[Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Eligibility, Entitlement and Planning Your Leave > Supplement with Paid Time Off]
If you need additional time after your Parental Leave:

- You may utilize [GitLab's Flexible Paid Time Off](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto) policy with manager coordination. If business critical deadlines will be missed, your Manager may ask you to change the dates.
- Discuss this with your manager following standard PTO guidelines (double the amount of notice as time requested).
- Submit PTO dates in Workday by selecting "Paid Time Off" and notify the Absence Management team.

You may not extend paid parental leave through the use of Paid [Caregiver Sick Time](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#caregiver-sick-time), unless you have a family member with a serious health condition.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
I don't know based on the handbook.
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
